property_summary: After any call to newGrantProposal(...) the contract's proposalCount increases by exactly 1 from its prior value (i.e., postCount == preCount + 1); the mutant that increments proposalCount after storing data emits a proposalCount that is off-by-one for the emitted event and stored entries and thus can violate this property for some inputs.

For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount), the contract's public proposalCount increases by at least 1 (postCount > preCount); the mutant that increments proposalCount after using it can leave proposalCount unchanged relative to expectations when observed via public getter/event ordering and thus violates this monotonic increase for some inputs.

For any (recipient, amount) the NewProposal event's proposalID equals the contract's proposalCount after the call; the mutant emits the event with an off-by-one ID relative to the stored public proposalCount for some inputs, so this rule distinguishes them.

For any caller address and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) leaves the contract's public proposalCount equal to the number emitted in the NewProposal event (i.e., the proposalCount getter reflects the ID emitted) — the mutant that increments proposalCount after storing data emits an event where the emitted proposalID does not match the post-call public proposalCount for some inputs, breaking this correspondence.

For any caller and any (recipient, amount) inputs, after calling newGrantProposal the contract's public proposalCount is strictly greater than the proposalCount value that was used to index the stored mapPID_grant entry (i.e., mapPID_grant was written at index oldCount and proposalCount returns oldCount+1), and the mutant that increments proposalCount before/after differently will make these differ for some inputs.

After calling newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) once from any caller, the reference contract increments proposalCount by exactly 1 (so proposalCount is previous+1); the mutant increments by 2, so for some fuzzed initial proposalCount the resulting proposalCount will differ and the property will fail.

For any initial state and any inputs, calling newGrantProposal increments proposalCount by exactly 1 (so newCount == oldCount + 1); the mutant that increments by 2 will violate this for some inputs, causing proposalCount to differ from old+1.

After calling newGrantProposal(...) the reference contract always increments proposalCount (so proposalCount increases by 1 from its prior value), whereas the mutant that omits the increment can leave proposalCount unchanged for some inputs (fuzzer will find one).

For any caller and any inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) on the correct contract always increases proposalCount by 1 (so proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant that removed the increment leaves proposalCount unchanged for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any grant params, after calling newGrantProposal the reference contract's proposalCount increases by exactly 1 from its prior value (i.e. proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant resets proposalCount to 0 at start, so for some inputs the observed proposalCount_after != proposalCount_before + 1 (e.g. when proposalCount_before != 0).
